books.title: Infiniment Moyen et plus si infinités dans les limites finies d'une édition minimaliste
books.author: Marc-Antoine Mathieu
books.review: The smallest (actually readable) book on earth is an 80-page graphic novel about the immensity of our infinite universe. A creative masterpiece and a unique reading experience.

books.title: Charlie Chaplin: My Autobiography
books.author: Charlie Chaplin
books.review: The autobiography of one of the most extraordinary artists. A captivating life but a book that reads like of succession of selected events without enough introspection (his parenting life is completely omitted). The narrative never feels as inspiring as it could have been.

books.title: L'art et la manière d'aborder son chef de service pour lui demander une augmentation
books.author: Georges Perec
books.review: A short book without punctuation that reads like one long sentence, unfolding like a flowchart illustrating the stupidity of bureaucracy. I found the book challenging to read. It's undeniably original but I don't know what to think about it.

books.title: Efficient Go
books.author: Bartlomiej Plotka
books.review: The author spends a great deal of time explaining how CPUs and memory work at the expense of diving deeper into Go-specific performance challenges. Personally, I find _Systems Performance_ by Brendan Gregg to be a more comprehensive and practical resource, even for junior Go developers who might be more interested by _Efficient Go_.

books.title: Working Effectively with Unit Tests
books.author: Jay Fields
books.review: If _XUnit Test Patterns_ gives you the full toolbox for mastering unit testing, _Working Effectively with Unit Tests_ provides an opiniated approach to use those tools in practice. A great contribution and a short book to share with your team to spark discussions and help you make intentional choices about how you test.

books.title: Who: The A Method for Hiring
books.author: Geoff Smart, Randy Street

books.title: On the Shortness of Life
books.author: Seneca
books.review: It's always eye-opening to understand that people have always operated the same way and "modern" problems aren't so. A short read that's best appreciated if you are already familiar with Stoic philosophy.
